summary: One small correction: Emil Makovicky is now described as a crystallographer at the University of Copenhagen rather than 'Danish', which I couldn't confirm. Everything else, including Lu's quotations, the 1453 Darb-i Imam figures and Cromwell's objection, checked out.

changes.after: Emil Makovicky, a crystallographer at the University of Copenhagen, had already
changes.why: Makovicky's base at the University of Copenhagen is documented, but no source I found gives his nationality as Danish.

notes: 'Scrolls like this served as training manuals' follows the AAAS/EurekAlert release. The Wikipedia page on the Topkapı Scroll suggests it may instead have been a record of tiling work rather than a workshop reference; the story's wording is supported, but scholars differ.

The Bielefeld Tilings Encyclopedia, following Necipoğlu, lists six girih shapes (two convex hexagons); Lu and Steinhardt's set, which the story uses, has five. Not an error, just two ways of counting.
Lu's 'Lu found no evidence the tiles were made... templates' line matches Philip Ball's Nature report: Lu said 'we speculate they were', to be used as templates.
'Thousands of photographs' is supported by a 2007 report reprinted at amaana.org; Aramco World says 'hundreds'. The story's countries match the AAAS release.
The rabbit hole's furtherReading link is the same PDF as the first source; counted as a separate link check. The Cromwell Springer link was confirmed via its DOI address.
